paper_metadata.title: DocOIE: A Document-level Context-Aware Dataset for OpenIE
paper_metadata.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL-IJCNLP 2021
paper_metadata.abstract: Open Information Extraction (OpenIE) aims to extract structured relational tuples (subject, relation, object) from sentences. Existing solutions perform extraction at sentence level, without referring to any additional contextual information. The paper introduces DocOIE, an expert-annotated document-level context-aware OpenIE dataset containing 800 sentences from 80 documents in healthcare and transportation domains, and proposes DocIE, a document-level context-aware OpenIE model. DocIE uses pre-trained BERT to encode source sentences with document context, segment tags to distinguish source and context, and additional transformer encoder layers for the source sentence. Experiments show that incorporating document-level context improves OpenIE performance.

problem_addressed: The paper addresses the lack of document-level context in existing sentence-level OpenIE systems and datasets. Without surrounding sentences, OpenIE may misinterpret part-of-speech and syntactic ambiguities, miss contextual information, or produce incorrect tuple boundaries. The objective is to create a context-aware benchmark and model that use surrounding document sentences to improve relational tuple extraction.

methodology.description: DocIE treats a document as a source sentence plus a symmetric window of surrounding context sentences. It concatenates source and context representations with trainable word and segment embeddings, uses bottom BERT blocks to model semantic interactions, keeps only the source representation, and applies additional top transformer blocks. A CopyAttention-style encoder-decoder then generates variable-length relational tuples, using a copying mechanism because tuple arguments and relations are usually input sub-spans. The training data are pseudo-labeled by traditional OpenIE systems selected on the expert-annotated DocOIE evaluation set.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: No domain ontology or fixed relation schema is used. The task is open-domain extraction of relational tuples represented as subject, relation, and object.

input_output.input_granularity: A source sentence together with a configurable window of surrounding sentences from the same document; training uses full document collections for pseudo-label generation.
input_output.output_representation: Open relational tuples in (subject, relation, object) form; these tuples are directly usable as graph facts but the paper does not construct a complete knowledge graph.

datasets: DocOIE evaluation dataset: 800 expert-annotated sentences from 80 patent documents, 40 healthcare and 40 transportation, containing 2,122 relational tuples
DocOIE training dataset: 2,400 patent documents, 1,200 per domain, used for pseudo-label bootstrapping

metrics: CaRB scorer metrics: AUC, precision, recall, and F1
Annotation consistency: tuple-level precision, recall, and F1
Error-analysis percentages for incompleteness, incorrect boundaries, redundant extractions, and grammatical errors
baselines: DocIE without the top transformer layer
evaluation.setting: Evaluation is performed on the DocOIE expert-annotated evaluation dataset using the CaRB scorer. Traditional systems are evaluated directly; neural baselines are trained with alternative pseudo-label sets generated by traditional OpenIE systems. DocIE uses context window size 5 for healthcare and 4 for transportation. The paper also evaluates window sizes 1–6 and conducts a qualitative case study plus error analysis on 50 randomly selected sentences.

value: DocIE with the top transformer achieved the best reported AUC and F1 in both domains: healthcare AUC 47.4 and F1 60.8; transportation AUC 38.5 and F1 56.9.
DocIE without the top transformer was second best in both domains: healthcare AUC 47.1 and F1 60.3; transportation AUC 38.5 and F1 56.4.
Against the strongest sentence-level neural baseline CopyAttention+BERT, DocIE with transformer improved F1 by 1.0 point in healthcare (60.8 vs. 59.8) and 0.8 point in transportation (56.9 vs. 56.1).
Annotation consistency between the two experts was 89.9 average F1, with precision 87.7 and recall 92.2.
The context-window study found optimal window size 5 for healthcare and 4 for transportation; larger windows may introduce noise.

evidence.excerpt: DocIE w transformer: Healthcare AUC 47.4, Prec 74.4, Rec 51.3, F1 60.8; Transportation AUC 38.5, Prec 56.0, Rec 57.5, F1 56.9.
CopyAttention+BERT: Healthcare AUC 46.8, F1 59.8; Transportation AUC 38.3, F1 56.1.
Average 87.7 precision, 92.2 recall, 89.9 F1.

value: Author claim: DocOIE provides document-level context and 800 expert-annotated sentences, substantially expanding expert-annotated OpenIE evaluation data relative to the datasets summarized by the authors.
Experimental result: DocIE with document context outperformed the evaluated sentence-level systems on the reported AUC and F1 metrics in both domains.
Review-level inference: The benchmark exposes context-dependent ambiguities and includes both domain diversity and document-level context, making it suitable for testing context-aware extraction.

DocIE w transformer achieves the best AUC and F1 in both domains.
The documents contain rich syntactic structures.

value: Experimental result: DocIE fails to cover at least one key phrase in 28% of the sampled sentences.
Experimental result: 27% of extractions have incorrect argument or relation boundaries, 15% of sentences contain redundant extractions, and 13% of extractions contain grammatical errors.
Author-reported weakness: DocIE is trained using pseudo labels produced by traditional sentence-level OpenIE models that do not use document context.

Review-level inference: The evaluation corpus is restricted to formally written patent documents in healthcare and transportation, so transfer to other document types is not established in this paper.
Review-level inference: The model outputs tuples but does not perform entity linking, ontology alignment, graph construction, validation, or updating.

The paper leaves unresolved how to train context-aware neural OpenIE without pseudo labels generated by context-free traditional systems.
